task: Owner decisions SL-N12 (promote), SL-N6 (cargo feature), SL-N5 (new FFT dependency); unify the side threads (dynamical systems, singular/algebraic geometry, Fourier/involution/convolution, algebraic topology) into a numerical-analysis foundation and implement the optimization it yields
objective: A structure-exact RODAS5P stage solver with certificates, built on one theory of the stage operator W(z) = zI - J, plus the three approved owner decisions.

environment.toolchain: stable 1.97.0 via RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable (pinned 1.94.1 not installable through the proxy)

stages.title: Symmetry: Z_np block diagonalization and the two involutions
Topology: Hodge form, H^0, stage mass identity, linear invariants of RODAS5P
Singular geometry: stage-pencil locus, inertia certificate, pole chart singularity
Dynamics: A-contractivity, Gershgorin spectral bound, stiffness certificate
Stage lattice revisited: width from irreducible blocks inside a stage
SL-N12: FixedWidth2 fixed-offset arithmetic in the protected banded driver; facade (2,2) rule; dense twins accept FixedWidth2
SL-N6: research-gates feature with self dev-dependencies
SL-N5: rustfft dependency and the separable stage solver (sphere, box)
SL-N5 diagnostics: whole solves and stage solves
Validation: suites, lint, format, run verifier

claims.claim: The longitude DFT block-diagonalizes the sphere heat operator into tridiagonal blocks depending on m only through cos(2 pi m/np).
A L is symmetric negative semidefinite and ker L = constants (dim H^0 = 1).
Non-positive Thomas pivots of the mode systems count the eigenvalues of J at or above z (Sylvester).
Stage mass identity (z - c) M(x) = M(b) holds to round-off for separable solves.
Separable stage solves are backward stable: max backward error 3.4e-16 over 7 grids and z in [1e-3, 1e4].
Whole IVPs on the separable route match a dense matrix-exponential reference (errors 6.6e-11 to 1.2e-10 at rtol 1e-8) and conserve the area mass to 4.3e-16.
The separable route conserves mass better than the shipped matrix-free route.
claims.evidence: shipped drift 1.4e-16 to 4.5e-15 at the same tolerances; no advantage observed

claims.claim: Verified mode corrects a ring-dependent decay declared as one mean rate (2.22 corrections per solve, 63 attempts, error 5.2e-11); the trusted solve of the same mismatch needs 819 attempts.

Host diagnostic: separable whole solves are 88-355x faster than the shipped matrix-free route (32x64, 64x128) at comparable achieved error; separable stage solves are 109-131x faster than GMRES with the longitude preconditioner on 32x64, 64x128 and 128x256.
FixedWidth2 with fixed offsets returns the Indexed/Slices bits, pivots, errors and counted work, including under pivoting in every column and singular columns.
Promoting FixedWidth2 changes 76 route labels and no state bit or counter in the golden files; host wall ratio 0.769 (n=1e4), 0.776 (n=1e5).
The facade builds without research-gates; 24 modules and 19,750 lines leave the default build; integrator library release build 43.2 s vs 60.5 s.
The eight RODAS5P stages can run in parallel.
The Gershgorin stiffness certificate selects the cheaper of DOPRI5 and the separable route.
A field-of-values certificate replaces inertia for advection.

decisions.detail: band (2,2) only; other narrow bands stay on Indexed per the V22 width scan
five modules reclassified to the default build (kill fallback)

decisions.commit: the commit that adds this file
decisions.detail: route opt-in through VigilODE::solve_separable; promotion waits for KS-N3

failures.what: Dense output on a JVP problem is refused by the facade's validation (JvpWithMassOrDenseOutput) before the separable refusal; the test was adjusted to accept the earlier typed refusal.
The shipped matrix-free route at 128x256 did not finish three repetitions within about 26 minutes on the host; no median recorded.
Unpreconditioned GMRES did not converge within 3000 Arnoldi vectors at 128x256, h = 0.1 (stage diagnostic); recorded as converged=false.
Pinned toolchain 1.94.1 not installable; stable 1.97.0 used for every command.
